finding.title: Fix the self-comparison assertion in firestore_listener_source_test.dart:153 — expect(x, equals(x)) always passes
finding.why: Comparing a value to itself is always true regardless of what orderField holds. The test's own comment states the intent — verify 'every wired collection... must carry an explicit, recognised field' via the actual order field passed to listenToCollection — and the preceding expect (checking FirestoreListenerSource.orderFields[entry.collection] is not null) does real work, but this second line adds nothing. If a future change wires the wrong orderField to a collection (e.g. swaps two entries in the orderFields map), this test cannot catch it, undermining the FB-2-adjacent guarantee that every listener sorts by its intended recency field.
finding.recommendation: Change to expect(entry.orderField, equals(FirestoreListenerSource.orderFields[entry.collection])) so the assertion checks the actual call-site value against the expected map entry.
acceptance_criteria: Deliberately wiring the wrong orderField constant to one collection in the source makes the test fail red

finding.title: Use the existing useLocalDayClock seam instead of DateTime.now() in sync_orchestrator_test.dart resume-throttle tests
finding.why: SyncOrchestratorImpl itself reads the clock through the injectable DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() (backed by useLocalDayClock/resetLocalDayClock, built specifically so 'tests can swap it' per date_utils.dart), but these two resume-throttle tests compute their seeded SharedPreferences timestamp from the real system clock instead. The 30s-vs-5min and 10min-vs-5min margins are wide enough that this isn't currently flaky, but it's an unnecessary wall-clock dependency the rest of the suite's own convention exists specifically to avoid, and it silently stops being safe if the throttle window is ever tightened close to a minute.
finding.recommendation: Call useLocalDayClock(fixedClock) in setUp and compute recentMs/oldMs as fixed offsets from the pinned clock, matching the DateTimeFactory convention used elsewhere in the suite.
acceptance_criteria: Resume-throttle tests no longer call DateTime.now()
Tests still pass with useLocalDayClock pinned to an arbitrary fixed instant

finding.title: Split app_theme.dart's duplicated _lightTheme/_darkTheme builders to bring the file under the 400-line AG-3 ceiling

evidence.quote: return const Color(0xFF7C3AED);  // == curriculumMussar, not referenced
return const Color(0xFF0EA5A0);  // == curriculumNach, not referenced

finding.why: At 687 lines this is the largest hand-written file in the batch (72% over the 400-line ceiling). The excess is structural duplication, not density: _lightTheme (202-441) and _darkTheme (447-686) build near-identical ButtonStyle/ChipTheme/CheckboxTheme/etc. trees, differing only in which colour tokens are plugged in (e.g. elevatedButtonTheme at :254-269 vs :499-514 are structurally identical). Any shape/radius/elevation change (e.g. card corner radius) must be hand-applied in both 240-line blocks with nothing to catch a miss — the two navigationBarTheme indicator alphas (0.12 vs 0.18) show the blocks already diverge in small ways. Separately, getCurriculumColor re-literals 0xFF7C3AED/0xFF0EA5A0 for mishnehTorah/tanach instead of referencing the already-declared curriculumMussar/curriculumNach constants two lines above — a future rebrand of either constant silently stops covering its look-alike case.
finding.recommendation: Extract a shared theme-shape builder parameterized by ColorScheme/accent/surface tokens so _lightTheme/_darkTheme stop hand-duplicating widget-theme trees; reference curriculumMussar/curriculumNach by name in getCurriculumColor instead of repeating their hex values.
acceptance_criteria: app_theme.dart line count ≤400 (AG-3 repo-wide line-count audit passes for this file).
getCurriculumColor's mishnehTorah/tanach cases reference curriculumMussar/curriculumNach (or a new distinct named constant, with a comment on the intentional pairing) rather than inline hex.
flutter_test golden/widget tests for light and dark theme (if any exist) still pass after the refactor.

finding.title: Retire or theme-align text_styles.dart's AppTextStyles, which hardcodes Roboto and diverges from AppTheme's Plus Jakarta Sans
finding.rule: Fowler duplication / dead code (no direct rule ID)

evidence.quote: // NOTE: 'Noto Sans Hebrew' font files must be placed in assets/fonts/ and

finding.why: AppTheme.textTheme (the app's real Material typography, wired into every themed widget via Theme.of(context)) uses GoogleFonts Plus Jakarta Sans; AppTextStyles is a second, parallel static typography table hardcoding 'Roboto' with no colour/brightness awareness. It is consumed directly (bypassing Theme) by lib/features/content_browsing/presentation/screens/text_display_screen.dart — a churn-hotspot screen — at 6 call sites, meaning that screen's text visibly renders in a different typeface family than the rest of the themed app. 'Roboto' also isn't a bundled font asset (only Noto Sans Hebrew is declared in pubspec.yaml), so the family isn't even guaranteed cross-platform (no Roboto on iOS). The file's own comment claiming the Hebrew font 'must be placed in assets/fonts/... until then' is stale — pubspec.yaml:211-222 already bundles all 5 Noto Sans Hebrew weights. getTextDirection/getStyleForContent (lines 146-164) have zero callers anywhere outside their own test file.
finding.recommendation: Either retire AppTextStyles in favour of Theme.of(context).textTheme at its 2 call sites, or derive it from the active theme/GoogleFonts.plusJakartaSans* instead of a hardcoded 'Roboto' literal so the two systems can't drift further; delete the 2 dead helper methods or wire them to a real caller; fix the stale font-availability comment.
acceptance_criteria: text_display_screen.dart and hebrew_text.dart render with the same font family as the rest of the themed app (Plus Jakarta Sans), verified by a widget test reading the resolved TextStyle.fontFamily.
getTextDirection/getStyleForContent removed (with their now-orphaned tests) or given a real caller.
Stale asset-bundling comment corrected or removed.

finding.title: Delete or wire up orphaned CurriculumIndicator and TrackProgressBar widgets (zero production callers)
finding.rule: Dead code (Fowler) — no direct rule ID

evidence.quote: // 207 lines exercising a widget with 0 production imports
// 98 lines exercising a widget with 0 production imports

finding.why: Repo-wide grep for `CurriculumIndicator(` and `TrackProgressBar(` finds zero matches outside each widget's own definition file. Together with their dedicated test files this is ~475 lines exercising no reachable code path — CI pays for it every run, and a maintainer searching for 'curriculum badge' or 'progress bar' will find and reuse an abandoned component instead of whatever superseded it (TrackProgressBar's own docstring says 'track-type display has been removed per product rules', confirming it's a leftover from a removed feature).
finding.recommendation: Delete both widgets and their test files, or if a near-term feature needs them, wire them into a real screen and note the ticket in a doc comment.
acceptance_criteria: Either both widget files + their test files are removed, or each has ≥1 production caller confirmed by grep.
`flutter analyze` / build stays green after removal (no orphaned imports).
